o1.biggest_mistake: The brand search forecast jumps to about 25 ROAS (from 17) and $455,000 value on $18,000, which looks optimistic and may overstate expected profit; the title strings are long and some wording (e.g. 'Women's Machine Washable Pointed Toe Flat') drifts from the brand's plain, warm voice.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: A more defensible brand forecast (conservative and base shown separately), tighter voice-checked title patterns, and a one-line explanation of how the reserve rule protects profit if lines underperform.

o2.biggest_mistake: It changes many things at once and adds a $21,000 regional test in the same 30 days, which muddies the read and the owner may not be able to attribute results; the schedules and tables are denser and harder to scan.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: A clearer, simpler one-page timeline and a cleaner separation between the core plan and the optional test so the owner knows what is proven versus what is being probed.

reason: Both are strong and I would use either. Output 2 wins slightly because it is more honest about falling reported revenue, more cautious on brand forecasting, and it tests the one thing I would worry about: whether cutting the cheap broad spend actually builds brand later.
